Two scientific layers and canonical ancestry

This reader covers 132 historical public canonical Agent-Oriented Software Engineering properties. The canonical study reconciles two complete antecedents; it is not an extra set to add to them. Antecedent A's 113 and B's 83 property rows map into the canonical 132. The source/source-count distinction also matters: the canonical source table has 124 work/edition records. Historical canonical report

The separately accepted AMA-L3 scientific subject has SHA-256 d60a32e34fc19d30f4b41272a1883a514daebec22196f448b3528b87b80f25fa and again selects 132 property identities. Its exact current source repairs, new adjudications and independent review findings are retained privately with the accepted subject. They are not silently applied to the original rows. SOURCE_MAP.json records the four-unit bindings. AMA-DISCLOSE-AMA-L3 remains PENDING.

What AOSE contributes

Agent-Oriented Software Engineering uses intentional responsibilities, goals, roles, interactions and organizations as subjects of requirements, analysis, design, implementation and change. It is broader than an agent runtime and different from using an agent to generate code. A strategic actor in a requirements model need not become a runtime agent. Conventional services and objects remain legitimate implementations when they meet the actual obligations. Historical public intake

The genealogy includes intentional programming and BDI foundations; actor/goal/dependency requirements; Gaia's role-oriented analysis and design; Tropos; MaSE/O-MaSE; Prometheus; compositional and knowledge-oriented methods; method engineering; public commitments; and later temporal, normative and generative hybrids. These are distinct methodological choices. A shared name or later framework branding does not establish full inheritance or a single compulsory lifecycle. Canonical reconciliation retains each A/B ancestry, its actual contribution and source ceiling. Historical coverage · Canonical reconciliation

The first sharp predicate is affected-stakeholder validation, C001: diagrams do not establish that all relevant people or dependencies were discovered. C002 connects requirements to acceptance; C006/007 distinguish delegation from an actor's current practical ability and permission; C020–025 concern roles, holders, organization and progress. A role can be present while the incumbent lacks capacity or authority. A valid organizational successor can still lose a predecessor's live obligation. C001–C011, C020–C025, C105

Interaction engineering must keep meaning, authentication, authorization, public obligations and external effect distinct. C036 rejects inaccessible private mental states as a sufficient public-compliance test; C037 preserves a separately guarded controlled/private-state branch. Their different polarities survive the canonical population. A norm or contract can define a responsibility without causing performance. A timeout can leave an effect uncertain, and retries can duplicate effects. C033–C043, C109

Assurance and composition have specific subjects

A model proof establishes its scoped proposition under the model's premises. A transformation preserves a specified relation between supported representations. A test supplies evidence at its oracle and observation scope. None establishes the legitimacy of the requirement, every environment assumption or physical enactment by mere coexistence. Conversely, an adequate atomic interface can provide a useful warrant without a second independent implementation. C058–C061, C081–C098

C086's compatible-support criterion requires the relevant warrants to join the same subject, principal, action, configuration and acceptance context. Correctly authorizing a refund to B does not meet A's distinct requirement. Pairwise satisfiable fragments need not have a common global witness; shared resource budgets can fail after individually feasible tasks are combined. An adequate direct check can discharge a small join, and conventional implementation remains a valid branch. These are bounded analytical distinctions rather than a new universal proof system. C054–C064, C079, C086 and canonical composition

Change and operation require actual consumers. A log no decision maker can use is not complete feedback. A changed premise can invalidate dependent evidence while leaving independent evidence intact. Changing role holders does not automatically transfer promises. C103/105/106 separate those obligations, with selective revalidation and omission when no affected dependency exists. Historical ledger

Generated roles and plans retain external obligations

The canonical population sharply distinguishes C123's retained role-contract boundary, C131's rejected prompt/contract equivalence and C132's rejected claim that role prompts alone constitute AOSE. C125 preserves actual tool authority. C129 concerns operational planning semantics. C130 concerns responsiveness while generation is pending; the source-grounded guidance is not a general response-time, fairness or deadline guarantee. These meanings are not interchangeable. C123–C132 · Historical public intake

Alternatives, negatives and remaining science

Ten historical configuration branches range from conventional software and AO analysis with ordinary execution to BDI, cooperative organization, public commitments, adaptive organization, specialized cooperative/holonic arrangements, stronger assurance, generative hybrids and minimum coherent engineering. These are guarded choices, not a checklist to instantiate together. Complete-method superiority remains unresolved in two distinct rows: C119 for the evolved configuration family and C120 for broad complete AOSE methods. Local successes, source counts and benchmark reuse do not settle either; absence of superiority evidence is not evidence that every mechanism is inferior. Canonical composition · C119/120

Canonical reconciliation admits no distinct new induced property. Its retained relation bundles and negative candidate decisions remain useful scientific outputs. Historical duplicate names and nested ancestral representations do not multiply independent mechanisms. The row reader retains A/B ancestry, canonical disposition and criterion, including negative, contested and unresolved records. The full nested originals remain in the immutable public corpus. Canonical reconciliation

Separate native responsibility

Published, canonically unallocated R0043 / #232 has a separate bounded EAOSE-132 documentary receiving record and an embedded AMA-continuation receiving scope. Neither closes the other simply through sharing an issue. The native source preserves original, older target, later prepared target and actual documentary decisions as separate layers. Runtime implementation is not earned by a route or property count. Existing qualification

The AMA-L3 rough responsibility focuses on exact requirements/implementation/evidence correspondence, live responsibility during change and the current native consumer. R002D/#197 retains systems/interfaces/model-credibility ownership; R0037/#211 retains whole control composition; R0033/#207, R0035/#209 and R0036/#210 preserve their own authority/join/lane boundaries. R001F/#158 governs any later authorized executor-ready residual. Owner map · Four rough responsibilities

Reconciliation
Both procedures elicit and challenge the affected-actor boundary rather than infer validity from a goal diagram. A-042 explicitly restates A-001 and contributes ancestry, not another mechanism. Development
B-005 bundles threat/security traceability, delegation legitimacy and effective capability. Its delegation/permission part maps here; its threat-to-test part and point-of-use capacity part map separately. A-005 explicitly distinguishes assigning a responsibility from legitimately granting authority. This row does not acquire all security claims of the B bundle.
Evolved form at historical freeze
Separate a request, an assignment, a commitment and an authorisation; check who can create, transfer or revoke obligations and operational powers.
Problem
One actor acts or promises on behalf of another.
Mechanism
Separate a request, an assignment, a commitment and an authorisation; check who can create, transfer or revoke obligations and operational powers.
Trigger and context
One actor acts or promises on behalf of another.
Preconditions
DATA: Actual affected actors and their accounts; proposed goals/dependencies, constraints, legitimacy and observable acceptance information.; PROPERTY_DEPENDENCIES: EAOSE-C001; EAOSE-C004; SPECIFIC_PRECONDITIONS: Identified principal and scope; externally meaningful authority, not merely a role label.
Decision or consumer
Principal grants or withholds powers; delegate acts within scope; counterpart receives the public obligation where relevant.
Authority boundary
Principal grants or withholds powers; delegate acts within scope; counterpart receives the public obligation where relevant.
Communication or interaction
Communicate the decision-relevant result to its actual consumer: Principal grants or withholds powers; delegate acts within scope; counterpart receives the public obligation where relevant. The operative evidence is: An action or obligation can be linked to valid standing, scope and revocation state. This is not a requirement for a new message protocol when an existing shared representation suffices.
Observable criterion
An action or obligation can be linked to valid standing, scope and revocation state.
Nontrigger or cheaper adequate path
A direct approved call inside one trust boundary may avoid a delegation protocol while retaining permission checks.
Historical disposition
STRONGLY_RETAINED
Failure modes
Mental intention, capability and normative obligation can each be mistaken for permission.
Criticism

Contrary evidence

Assumption sensitivity
REQUIRED: Identified principal and scope; externally meaningful authority, not merely a role label.; CHANGED_ASSUMPTION_TEST: Reassess support when these prerequisites change; the observable consequence remains: An action or obligation can be linked to valid standing, scope and revocation state.
Unresolved questions
Under what actual conditions does this mechanism improve its proposed payoff enough to justify its cost? Prevents unapproved action and orphaned obligations; does not guarantee the authorised action succeeds.

Check both the practical ability and current permission to perform a consequential operation at the point of use.
Trigger and context
A role or agent may be allocated work it cannot or may no longer perform.

Reconciliation
A-100 already requires compatible support before transferring a composed guarantee.
